title: Irreducible components
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space. $X$ is *irreducible* if it is nonempty and, whenever $X=Z_1\cup Z_2$ with $Z_1,Z_2$ closed, $X=Z_1$ or $X=Z_2$; a subset is irreducible if it is so in the subspace topology. A subset $Z\subseteq X$ is an *irreducible component* of $X$ if it is a maximal irreducible subset of $X$ (such a $Z$ is closed). The irreducible components of a scheme are those of its underlying topological space.
